title: Blind Speed
tagline: Night, the North Sea, and three airspeeds that disagree.
history: Inspired by airliners whose pitot probes iced over or were blocked at night over the sea — a 1996 departure and a 2009 cruise among them — where the crews lost control following unreliable instruments instead of flying pitch and power.
situation: 02:40, FL350 over the North Sea, 176 asleep in the back, thunderstorms around. The pitot probes ice over: the autopilot drops out and the airspeed goes wrong. There is no horizon out there.
failures: Pitot probes iced: the airspeed indications are unreliable
The ice clears after about two minutes
tips: Don't chase the speed tape. Fly pitch and power: about 2–3° nose up, thrust ~80 %
Wings level, small inputs — the aircraft was flying fine a moment ago
The altimeter and attitude are still good
A stall warning means lower the nose, not pull
limit_text: The crew never got the aircraft back into stable flight.

do.note: F/O: Speeds… we've lost the speeds! Unreliable airspeed — I have no idea what we're doing.
F/O: The speeds agree again — the probes have cleared.

objectives.text: Keep control for 2½ minutes: no stall, no overspeed, bank under 60°
